content_of_post_to_comment: On Wikipedia bias: First of all, we should all be extremely grateful that there is a small corner of the internet that really is dedicated to public service rather than the relentless war for ad revenue that otherwise prevails. Most topics are not politically contentious - Wikipedia is still extremely useful for those. However, yes, on politically contentious topics, Wikipedia remains useful, and will not lie to you, but it will perhaps give an editorialised version of the truth. In this sense it is neither better nor worse than the mainstream media, and a good deal better than “alternative” media. To the extent that bias exists, it is obviously slanted to the left. (And don't come at me with “reality has a left-wing bias”.) This is a simple selection effect - Wikipedia is a prosocial voluntary organisation, and people who volunteer for prosocial efforts skew left. What this isn't, and what many right-wing critics accuse it of being, is a conspiracy to seize a trusted information source to peddle a grand ideological narrative. Wikipedians are largely honest and try to be as fair as they can, but some unconscious bias is always going to seep through. Therefore the solution seems obvious - rather than moaning about it, conservatives should instead become Wikipedia editors - good-faith ones, working to improve the accessibility of information rather than pushing their own pet ideas. That's the way to undo the bias.
